name: Pakistani Samosa
description: Crisp Pakistani potato samosas with a firm ajwain-scented dough, cooled spiced filling and tightly sealed wrappers fried slowly for a flaky finish.
ingredients: 2 cups plain flour, plus a little for dusting
4 tbsp neutral oil for the dough
About 1/2 cup water for the dough, added gradually
3 medium potatoes, boiled, peeled and roughly mashed
1/2 tsp crushed red chilli, or to taste
2 tbsp flour mixed with a little water, for sealing
method: Rub the dough oil into the flour with the ajwain and measured salt until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add water gradually to form a firm, pliable dough, knead only until smooth, then cover and rest for about 30 minutes.

For the filling, heat the oil and bloom the cumin briefly. Add the green chillies and crushed red chilli, then fold in the potatoes and remaining salt. Cook briefly, finish with coriander and lemon juice and let the filling cool completely.

Divide the rested dough into equal balls. Roll each into a thin oval and cut it in half. Moisten a straight edge with flour paste, overlap to form a cone and press the seam firmly so there are no gaps.
Fill each cone without overpacking it, leave enough clean dough at the top to seal, then moisten and press the top edges tightly together. Keep assembled samosas covered while shaping the remainder.
Heat the frying oil over medium-low to medium heat. Add only a few samosas at a time and fry gently, turning occasionally, so the raw dough has time to become crisp before the exterior gets too dark.
Continue until evenly deep golden and crisp, then drain on a rack or absorbent paper without piling them tightly while hot. Serve warm with mint or tamarind chutney.
tips: A firm, rested dough makes a crisper wrapper than a soft, sticky dough.
Cool the potato filling before shaping, and seal every edge well to prevent leaks.
Fry gently in small batches; rapidly bubbling oil is too hot for raw samosa dough.
storage: Samosas are best fresh. Cool leftovers promptly, refrigerate covered and reheat with dry heat until thoroughly hot and crisp.
serving: Pair with green mint chutney or sweet tamarind chutney and a cup of chai.
